title: Being able to
canDo: I can turn any verb into its potential form: 食べる → 食べられる, 飲む → 飲める, する → できる, 来る → 来られる.
I can say what I can and can't do, in the present and the past: 漢字が読めます / きのうはねられませんでした.
I can choose the object particle for a potential verb (が, or を) and keep the other particles (で, に) as they are.
I can recognize the casual ら抜き forms (見れる, 来れる) and write the standard forms (見られる, 来られる).
I can say the same thing with 〜ことができる, in a more formal tone, and I know when each form sounds better.

blocks.t: Warm-up: say out loud the dictionary form of 10 Genki I verbs (飲みます → 飲む, 来ます → 来る…) and the type of each (る, う or irregular)
Vocabulary: tap 🔊 on each word and repeat it twice
Grammar: the 3 points, each with its examples read aloud and one 🔬
Lesson 13 video (block 6), only the potential part
Notebook homework + checking it against the answer key
Checklist (block 10) + write your questions in the lesson notebook

skills: The dictionary form of every verb, knowing whether each one is a る-verb, an う-verb or irregular (lessons 03-1 and 08-1). The potential form is built straight from it.
The ない form and the short past (lessons 08-1 and 09-1). The potential conjugates like a る-verb: 飲めない, 飲めた…
Contrastive は (lesson 03-2), which shows up a lot in negative sentences with the potential.
Sentences that describe nouns (lesson 09-2) and 〜たり〜たりする (lesson 11-1), which appear in two examples.
From Genki II on, sentences come without spaces and with more kanji. The kana reading is always shown next to them.

vocab.en: to drive (a car) (potential: 運転できる)
to make; to cook (food); to create
cooking; food, dish (ブラジル料理 = Brazilian food)
to put on, wear (a shirt, a coat, a kimono)
to play (the piano, the guitar): ピアノをひく
to get up, wake up (potential: 起きられる)
to ride, get on (a vehicle): 自転車にのる
can do, to be able to (it is the potential of する); with a noun, to know how: 日本語ができる
can / to be able to do… (a more formal tone)

grammar.title: Forming it: 食べられる, 飲める, できる, 来られる
grammar.gloss: the potential form: "can / be able to do"
grammar.explanation:
The potential form says what someone **can** do or **is able** to do: "I can swim", "I can get up at six", "you can eat this". English adds a separate word, "can". Japanese changes **the verb itself**. Always start from the **dictionary form** (lesson 08-1) and check the verb type.
• **る-verbs**: drop る and add **られる**. 食べ|る → 食べ|られる; 見る → 見られる; 起きる → 起きられる.
• **う-verbs**: change the final **u** to the **e** of the same kana row and add **る**. 飲む (nom**u**) → 飲める (nom**e**ru); 行く → 行ける; 話す → 話せる; 待つ → 待てる; 帰る → 帰れる; およぐ → およげる; あそぶ → あそべる. Verbs ending in う go to え: 買う → 買える; 歌う → 歌える.
• **Irregulars**: **する → できる** (運転する → 運転できる) and **来る → 来られる** (こられる).
• **The potential is a new る-verb.** Once you have formed it, it conjugates like 食べる: 飲める → 飲めます (I can drink it), 飲めません (I can't), 飲めました (I could, I managed to), 飲めませんでした (I couldn't), 飲めない, 飲めた.
• **ら抜き ("ら dropped")**: in casual speech, many people drop the ら from る-verbs and from 来る: 見れる, 食べれる, 来れる (これる). You will hear this all the time in conversations, anime and games. But the standard form, the one in Genki, in tests and in writing, is **見られる, 食べられる, 来られる**. Understand both; write the standard one.
• In the sentence, the potential verb is the **PREDICATE**, at the end. Read from it: "can you get up?" → at what time? → every morning.
grammar.structure: る: [stem] + られる · う: u → e + る · する → できる · 来る → 来られる

examples.jp: ペドロさんはポルトガル語と英語と日本語が話せます。
examples.kana: ペドロさんはポルトガルごとえいごとにほんごがはなせます。
examples.romaji: Pedoro-san wa porutogarugo to eigo to nihongo ga hanasemasu.
examples.en: Pedro can speak Portuguese, English and Japanese.

examples.jp: 毎朝六時に起きられますか。— いいえ、六時には起きられません。
examples.kana: まいあさろくじにおきられますか。— いいえ、ろくじにはおきられません。
examples.romaji: Maiasa rokuji ni okiraremasu ka. — Iie, rokuji ni wa okiraremasen.
examples.en: Can you get up at six every morning? — No, I can't get up at six.

examples.jp: マリアさんは日曜日にアルバイトがあるので、パーティーに来られません。
examples.kana: マリアさんはにちようびにアルバイトがあるので、パーティーにこられません。
examples.romaji: Maria-san wa nichiyōbi ni arubaito ga aru node, pātī ni koraremasen.
examples.en: Maria has her part-time job on Sunday, so she can't come to the party.

pitfalls: う-verbs go to the え row, not the あ row: 行かれる ✗ → 行ける ✓. (行かれる does exist, but it is the passive voice, which comes in lesson 21-1.)
帰る, 入る, 知る and 走る look like る-verbs, but they are う-verbs: 帰られる ✗ → 帰れる ✓ (かえ|る → かえ|れる).
する becomes できる, and 来る becomes こられる, with こ: 運転しられる ✗ → 運転できる ✓; きられる ✗ → こられる ✓.
わかる already means "to understand, to be clear to me" and has no potential form: わかれる ✗ (that is a different word, "to part, break up"). "I can understand" = わかります ✓.
howToStudy: Make a table in your notebook with 12 verbs (4 る-verbs, 6 う-verbs, する and 来る) in three columns: dictionary → potential → potential + ません. Read it aloud, row by row, and highlight 帰る in color.

Tap 🔬 on example 2. The PREDICATE is 起きられますか; 毎朝 and 六時に both show up as TIME. Read it backwards: can you get up? → at what time? → every morning. In the answer, notice 六時には (also TIME): the に of clock time stayed and picked up a contrastive は.
Say out loud 5 things you can do and 3 you can't, all of them true: 自転車にのれます。ピアノはひけません。…
grammar.flag: Check in your Genki II that this lesson has these points in this order.

grammar.title: The object of the potential: が (and also を)
grammar.gloss: 日本語が話せます / 日本語を話せます
grammar.explanation:
With an ordinary verb, the object takes を: 日本語を話します. With the potential, the object very often takes **が** instead: 日本語**が**話せます. The reason: the sentence no longer tells about an action; it describes an **ability**, a state. Japanese likes が with states, as in すしが好きです (lesson 05-2).
• **It is not an absolute rule.** With the potential, **を also appears**, and many speakers use both: 日本語を話せます is not wrong. You will often see を in longer sentences, like the job ad in example 3. Genki and most textbooks present **が** as the standard. When in doubt, use が.
• **Only を can change.** The other particles stay as they are: 海**で**およげます (place), 友だち**に**会えます (who you meet), 自転車**に**のれます (what you ride), 一人**で**行けます (how).
• In negatives and contrasts, contrastive **は** (lesson 03-2) shows up a lot: 肉**は**食べられません = "meat, I can't eat" (other things, yes).
• できる also works on its own, with a noun: 日本語**が**できます ("I know Japanese"), 料理**が**できます ("I can cook"), テニスができます ("I can play tennis").
• Anatomy: in 漢字が読めます, 🔬 labels 漢字が as SUBJECT because of the が, but it is still **what you can read**. The person who reads is the topic, and it is often not even said.
grammar.structure: [object] が [potential] (standard) · [object] を [potential] (also used) · で, に… don't change

examples.jp: ルーカスさん、漢字が読めますか。— はい、少し読めます。
examples.kana: ルーカスさん、かんじがよめますか。— はい、すこしよめます。
examples.romaji: Rūkasu-san, kanji ga yomemasu ka. — Hai, sukoshi yomemasu.
examples.en: Lucas, can you read kanji? — Yes, I can read a little.

examples.jp: 父は、魚は食べられますが、肉は食べられません。
examples.kana: ちちは、さかなはたべられますが、にくはたべられません。
examples.romaji: Chichi wa, sakana wa taberaremasu ga, niku wa taberaremasen.
examples.en: My father can eat fish, but he can't eat meat.

examples.jp: ポルトガル語を話せる人をさがしています。
examples.kana: ポルトガルごをはなせるひとをさがしています。
examples.romaji: Porutogarugo o hanaseru hito o sagashite imasu.
examples.en: We're looking for someone who can speak Portuguese.

pitfalls: The switch applies only to the object. A place still takes で: 海がおよげます ✗ → 海でおよげます ✓.
With an ordinary verb, the object keeps を: 日本語が話します ✗ → 日本語を話します ✓. が only appears when the verb becomes potential (話せます).
を with the potential is not a mistake. If you hear 日本語を話せます, it is correct. Just don't use を with できる + noun: 日本語をできます ✗ → 日本語ができます ✓.
howToStudy: Read examples 1 and 3 aloud twice: once as written and once swapping the object particle (漢字を読めますか / ポルトガル語が話せる人). Both versions are correct. In the homework, use が, the book's form.

Tap 🔬 on example 2. 父は, 魚は and 肉は all show up as TOPIC: the last two are contrastive は (fish × meat). 食べられますが shows up as …BUT and closes the first half; 食べられません is the PREDICATE of the whole sentence.
Write 4 sentences about what you can and can't do in places you know, keeping the place particle: 図書館では話せません。この海ではおよげます。…

grammar.title: 〜ことができる: the more formal way
grammar.gloss: can / be able to do (the tone of rules, notices and written text)
grammar.explanation:
There is a second way to say "can": **dictionary form + ことが できる**. こと turns the action into a "thing" ("the act of swimming"), and できる says that this thing is possible. The meaning is practically the same as the potential.
• およげます = およぐことができます; 読めます = 読むことができます.
• **When to use it**: 〜ことができる sounds **more formal**, more like written text. It is very common in notices, rules, websites and ads: ここでは写真をとることができません. In everyday conversation, the potential is more common.
• **The particle**: inside the こと block, the object keeps **を**: 日本語**を**話す**こと**が できます. The が goes after こと, not after the object.
• With する-verbs, both forms live side by side: 運転することができます = 運転できます.
• A practical tip: if you freeze on a potential form in the middle of a conversation, 〜ことができます almost always saves you, because it only needs the dictionary form.
• In the sentence, [verb + こと] is **what is possible** (🔬 labels [verb + ことが] as SUBJECT), and できます is the **PREDICATE**. Read できます (or できません) first, then ask: what?
grammar.structure: [dictionary form] + ことが できます = [potential] + ます

examples.jp: このアプリで、日本のラジオを聞くことができます。
examples.kana: このアプリで、にほんのラジオをきくことができます。
examples.romaji: Kono apuri de, Nihon no rajio o kiku koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: With this app, you can listen to Japanese radio.

examples.jp: 図書館の中では、食べたり飲んだりすることができません。
examples.kana: としょかんのなかでは、たべたりのんだりすることができません。
examples.romaji: Toshokan no naka de wa, tabetari nondari suru koto ga dekimasen.
examples.en: Inside the library, you can't eat or drink. [lit. can't do things like eating and drinking]

examples.jp: マリアさんは着物を一人で着ることができます。
examples.kana: マリアさんはきものをひとりできることができます。
examples.romaji: Maria-san wa kimono o hitori de kiru koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: Maria can put on a kimono by herself.

pitfalls: こと is required: およぐができます ✗ → およぐことができます ✓.
Before こと comes the dictionary form, not the ます form: およぎますことができます ✗ → およぐことができます ✓.
Don't combine the two forms: およげることができます ✗. Use one or the other: およげます ✓ or およぐことができます ✓.
With friends, 〜ことができる in every sentence sounds stiff, like a rulebook. In casual speech, use the potential: あした来られる？ ✓.
howToStudy: Say the 3 examples of point a out loud again with 〜ことができます (話すことができます, 起きることができますか…) and notice how the tone becomes more formal.

Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🔬 Analyze: paste example 2. 図書館の中では shows up as PLACE, 食べたり and 飲んだり as THINGS LIKE, and することが as SUBJECT: that whole stretch is what is "not possible", and できません is the PREDICATE.
Invent 3 rules for your home or your workplace, as if they were signs, with 〜ことができません. Then say each one again with the potential, as if you were explaining it to a friend.
grammar.flag: The contrast with 〜ことができる is an addition of this course. Check whether your Genki II presents this form in this lesson; if it doesn't, treat this point as a bonus.

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook. Write the kanji you already know and the rest in kana. Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day. If you have the Genki II Workbook, do this lesson's exercises too.

tasks.prompt: Change each verb to the polite potential (〜ます). Before writing, decide the verb type: る, う or irregular.

items.note: る-verb: drop る and add られる. 食べれます is ら抜き, from casual speech.
う-verb: む (mu) → め (me) + る.
帰る looks like a る-verb, but it is an う-verb: かえ|る → かえ|れる.
With こ. 来れます (これます) is ら抜き.

tasks.prompt: Fill in the particle. Where the object can take either が or を, write the form Genki presents as the standard.

items.note: Object of the potential: が is the standard. を also occurs (日本語を話せます).
Place of the action: で doesn't change with the potential.

items.q: 一人で自転車＿のれます。
items.note: のる takes に (what you ride), and that doesn't change.

items.q: 日曜日は友だち＿会えません。
items.note: 会う takes に (who you meet), and the potential doesn't touch that.

items.q: ピアノ＿ひくことができます。
items.note: Inside the こと block, the object keeps を. The が comes after こと.

items.q: 肉＿食べられませんが、魚は食べられます。
items.note: Contrast: meat × fish. This is the contrastive は of lesson 03-2.

tasks.prompt: Translate into Japanese, using the potential (and 〜ことができる only where asked).

items.q: I can read hiragana and katakana, but I can't read kanji yet.

a.jp: ひらがなとカタカナは読めますが、漢字はまだ読めません。
a.kana: ひらがなとカタカナはよめますが、かんじはまだよめません。
a.romaji: Hiragana to katakana wa yomemasu ga, kanji wa mada yomemasen.

items.q: Can you come tomorrow at nine?

a.jp: あした九時に来られますか。
a.kana: あしたくじにこられますか。

a.jp: きのうの夜はねられませんでした。
a.kana: きのうのよるはねられませんでした。
a.romaji: Kinō no yoru wa neraremasen deshita.

items.note: ねる is a る-verb: ねられる. Past negative: 〜られませんでした.

a.jp: アナさんはブラジル料理が作れます。
a.kana: アナさんはブラジルりょうりがつくれます。
a.romaji: Ana-san wa burajiru ryōri ga tsukuremasu.

items.note: With を (ブラジル料理を作れます) it is also correct. ブラジル料理ができます works too.

items.q: Can I use a card at this store?

a.jp: この店でカードが使えますか。
a.kana: このみせでカードがつかえますか。
a.romaji: Kono mise de kādo ga tsukaemasu ka.

items.q: (on a sign) You can't ride a bicycle in this park. Use 〜ことができません.

a.jp: このこうえんでは自転車にのることができません。
a.kana: このこうえんではじてんしゃにのることができません。
a.romaji: Kono kōen de wa jitensha ni noru koto ga dekimasen.

items.note: It is a rule: that is why 〜ことができません fits.

tasks.prompt: You are having a めんせつ (interview) for an アルバイト at a store. Write 5 sentences about yourself: 2 things you can do, 1 thing you can't do yet, 1 saying which days you can work, and 1 with 〜ことができます. Then read them aloud, as if you were in the interview, and record yourself on your phone.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: ポルトガル語と英語が話せます。料理も作れます。でも、漢字はまだあまり読めません。月曜日と水曜日に働けます。土曜日も来ることができます。
a.kana: ポルトガルごとえいごがはなせます。りょうりもつくれます。でも、かんじはまだあまりよめません。げつようびとすいようびにはたらけます。どようびもくることができます。
a.romaji: Porutogarugo to eigo ga hanasemasu. Ryōri mo tsukuremasu. Demo, kanji wa mada amari yomemasen. Getsuyōbi to suiyōbi ni hatarakemasu. Doyōbi mo kuru koto ga dekimasu.
a.en: I can speak Portuguese and English. I can also cook. But I still can't read many kanji. I can work on Mondays and Wednesdays. I can come on Saturdays, too.

items.note: Check: 働く → 働ける (う-verb: く → け); the object takes が (or も, which replaces が); the negative uses contrastive は; and 来ることができます has the dictionary form before こと.

practice.what: Play normally, ideally in an N4-level area if you have reached one. Hunt the dialogues for potential verbs: endings in 〜える / 〜られる, できる, and the ら抜き forms (見れる, 来れる). When you find one, say out loud which dictionary verb it came from. Log the session in Immersion → Games and paste one of those lines into 🔬 Anatomy.
Drills → Conjugation: warm up with the dictionary form and the ない form, the base of the potential. Then Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🧱 Build from the end with example 3 of point a, starting from 来られません.

Write 4 true sentences in the Journal: 2 about what you can do and 2 about what you can't (with contrastive は). Open "Anatomy of what I wrote" and check that the potential verb ended up as the PREDICATE.
Tap 🔊 on each example in this lesson and repeat along 3 times. Notice the rhythm of 起きられません: お・き・ら・れ・ま・せ・ん is 7 equal beats. Don't swallow the ら.
Record your めんせつ (homework h4) in 40 seconds or less. Listen and check that every "I can" verb came out in the potential.

culture.title: アルバイト: part-time jobs
culture.body: In Japan, most university students have some kind of **アルバイト**, or just **バイト**: a part-time job paid by the hour. The word comes from the German *Arbeit* ("work"). The most common places are konbini, restaurants, izakaya, shops and cram schools, where many university students teach younger pupils. The hourly wage, the **じきゅう** (時給), is usually shown prominently in job ads, and the minimum wage is set by prefecture, so it varies from region to region. To get the job there is usually a short めんせつ, and many shops ask for a りれきしょ, a CV on a standard form, with a photo. International students need permission from the immigration office to work, and during the school term the limit is usually 28 hours a week.
culture.try: Rehearse a めんせつ out loud: answer 何曜日に働けますか。, 日本語が話せますか。 and 朝早く来られますか。 with the potential. At the end, say one thing you can't do yet, with contrastive は.

checklist: I can make the potential form of any verb without looking: る → られる, う → e + る, する → できる, 来る → 来られる.
I remember that 帰る is an う-verb: 帰れる.
I conjugate the potential like a る-verb: 飲めます, 飲めません, 飲めました, 飲めませんでした.
I use が (or を) for the object of the potential and keep で and に as they are: 海でおよげます.
I recognize 見れる and 来れる as casual ら抜き and I write 見られる and 来られる.
I can say the same thing with 〜ことができます, and I know it sounds more formal.
I did the homework, checked it against the answer key and redid what I got wrong.
If I have the Genki II Workbook: I did the Potential Verbs exercises.
